content.title: What are Enums & Inner Classes?
content.description: Enums are special Java types used to define a fixed set of constants, while Inner Classes are classes declared inside another class to improve encapsulation and logical grouping.

content.content: Java provides Enums to represent predefined constant values such as days of the week or user roles. Inner Classes allow one class to be nested inside another, making code more organized and improving encapsulation. Both are widely used in modern Java applications and frameworks.

content.title: Why Learn Enums & Inner Classes?
content.content: Enums improve type safety by replacing integer constants, while Inner Classes help organize related code, reduce namespace pollution, and enable better object-oriented design.
An enum defines a collection of named constants. Each enum constant is an object of the enum type, making enums much safer than using integer or string constants.

content.title: Creating an Enum
content.code:
enum Day {
    MONDAY,
    TUESDAY,
    WEDNESDAY,
    THURSDAY,
    FRIDAY,
    SATURDAY,
    SUNDAY
}

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: Enums provide compile-time type safety because only predefined constant values are allowed.

content.content: Enum constants can be assigned to variables and compared using the equality operator (==).

content.space_complexity: Minimal object overhead depending on implementation

content.title: Where are Enums & Inner Classes Used?

items.question: Spring Framework
items.answer: Enums represent application states and configuration values.

items.question: GUI Applications
items.answer: Anonymous inner classes handle button click events.

items.question: Banking Systems
items.answer: Enums define account types and transaction statuses.

items.question: Enterprise Applications
items.answer: Inner classes encapsulate helper functionality within classes.

content.title: Company Departments
content.content: Think of an enum as a list of fixed company departments like HR, Finance, and IT. An inner class is like a team that exists only within a department and works closely with it. Both help organize the company efficiently.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: Enums, values(), valueOf(), ordinal(), member inner classes, static nested classes, anonymous classes, local classes, and enum advantages are among the most frequently asked Java interview topics.

items.question: Should integers be used instead of enums?
items.answer: No. Enums provide type safety and make the code easier to understand.

items.question: Can a static nested class directly access non-static members of the outer class?
items.answer: No. It can directly access only static members unless it has an outer class object.

items.question: Are anonymous inner classes reusable?
items.answer: No. They are intended for one-time implementations.

content.title: Remember This
content.description: Enums represent a fixed set of constants with type safety, while Inner Classes improve encapsulation by grouping closely related classes together.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Enums are type-safe and support methods.
Inner classes are declared inside other classes.
Java supports member, static, local, and anonymous inner classes.
Anonymous inner classes are commonly used for event handling.
Enums and inner classes improve code organization and maintainability.
